definition: bands of colored light that appear in the night sky near the Earth's poles

collocations.example: Tourists travel north to watch the aurora.
The aurora appeared as green waves of light.

definition: a tool with a long curved blade used for cutting grass or crops by hand

collocations.example: The farmer swung his scythe through the wheat.
They cut the tall grass with a scythe.

definition: a sweet paste made from almonds and sugar, used to decorate cakes

collocations.example: The cake had a layer of marzipan on top.
She covered the fruitcake with marzipan.

definition: a very small mouse-like animal with a long pointed nose

collocations.example: A tiny shrew darted across the path.
Owls often hunt shrews at night.

definition: to start or introduce something again, especially a product or service

collocations.example: The company plans to relaunch the product next spring.
The brand was relaunched under a new name.

definition: a heavy base that supports a statue, column, or piece of furniture

collocations.example: The statue stood on a stone plinth.
The sculpture was mounted on a marble plinth.

definition: the activity of spreading a message, especially religious beliefs, to others

collocations.example: The group is known for its religious evangelism.
They spread their beliefs through evangelism.

definition: a mixture of two liquids, such as oil and water, that do not normally combine

collocations.example: Shaking the bottle helps the oil and vinegar form an emulsion.
The recipe creates a smooth, stable emulsion.

definition: the smallest number of people who must be present at a meeting before decisions can be made.

collocations.example: The committee could not reach a quorum, so they postponed the vote.
The bylaws set a quorum requirement of twenty voting members.

definition: a loose, comfortable outfit of a matching jacket and pants worn for sports or exercise.

collocations.example: She likes to wear a tracksuit when jogging in the park.
He pulled on a zip-up tracksuit before heading to the gym.

definition: a keyboard instrument, popular before the piano, whose strings are plucked to make sound.

collocations.example: She learned to play the harpsichord for the early music concert.
The small hall filled with delicate harpsichord music all evening.

definition: to repair or equip something, especially a ship or room, with new parts or fittings.

collocations.example: The company spent months to refit the old ship for passengers.
They decided to refit the kitchen with modern cabinets and appliances.

definition: careful to plan and save for the future, especially by setting money aside.

collocations.example: Her provident planning meant the family had savings for emergencies.
His provident habits helped him retire comfortably at sixty.

definition: an illness in which the tubes carrying air to the lungs become swollen and sore.

collocations.example: He developed bronchitis after a bad cold lingered for weeks.
Years of smoking left her with chronic bronchitis and a cough.

definition: to move something, or to move, with short quick movements from side to side.

collocations.example: The baby laughed when I began to waggle my fingers.
The happy dog started to waggle its tail at the door.

definition: a large snake that kills animals by wrapping around them and squeezing tightly.

collocations.example: The python coiled around the branch and waited silently for prey.
Visitors watched a giant python slide slowly across the glass tank.

definition: used in ordinary or familiar conversation rather than in formal speech or writing.

collocations.example: The textbook explained each colloquial expression that students might hear daily.
He learned colloquial English by chatting with friends after class.

definition: a machine that holds and turns wood or metal so it can be shaped with tools.

collocations.example: The trainee learned to operate a lathe safely in the workshop.
He shaped the chair legs on a wood lathe at home.

definition: to remove or prevent a difficulty or need so it no longer has to be dealt with.

collocations.example: A clear manual can obviate the need for constant staff training.
Careful planning may obviate many problems before the project even begins.

definition: to provide a country or group with weapons again, or to arm oneself once more.

collocations.example: The government moved quickly to rearm the nation after the war.
Neighboring states grew nervous when the country began to rearm.

definition: to promise to pay someone for any loss, damage, or injury they suffer.

collocations.example: The contract requires the supplier to indemnify the company against losses.
The insurer agreed to fully indemnify her for the flood damage.

definition: a sweater that you put on by pulling it over your head, with no front buttons.

collocations.example: She wore a warm pullover on the chilly autumn morning.
He bought a thick woolen pullover for the winter trip.

definition: so full of water that it is soaked, flooded, or too wet to use.

collocations.example: The match was canceled because the field was completely waterlogged.
Heavy rain caused the camping ground to become badly waterlogged.

definition: a wooden or metal frame used to support a table top, bridge, or platform.

collocations.example: They set up a long trestle table for the outdoor dinner.
The train slowed as it crossed the old wooden trestle bridge.

definition: a row of columns set at regular distances, usually supporting a roof or arches.

collocations.example: Tourists walked beneath the marble colonnade surrounding the ancient temple.
A long colonnade lined both sides of the grand courtyard.

definition: to greatly reduce the number of people living in an area.

collocations.example: War and famine began to depopulate the entire northern region.
Rural towns can rapidly depopulate when young people move to cities.

definition: second to last; immediately before the final one in a series.

collocations.example: The mystery deepens in the penultimate chapter of the novel.
She was eliminated in the penultimate round of the competition.

definition: a porch or covered entrance with a roof supported by columns at a building's front.

collocations.example: Guests gathered under the grand portico before the ceremony began.
The museum entrance featured a tall columned portico facing the street.

definition: a person or shop that makes or sells clothes, especially men's clothing.

collocations.example: He ordered a tailored suit from a trusted local clothier.
The fine clothier displayed wool coats in the shop window.

definition: a rude, rough, or aggressive man or boy who behaves badly.

collocations.example: A drunken lout shouted insults at passengers on the late train.
He later apologized for behaving like a lout at the party.

definition: having a good or helpful effect, often by teaching a useful lesson through difficulty.

collocations.example: The failed project was a salutary lesson about poor planning.
The warning had a salutary effect on the careless drivers.

definition: an imaginary creature in stories that can change from a person into a wolf

collocations.example: In the legend, the man turns into a werewolf at night.
They watched an old werewolf movie on Halloween.

definition: a common light plastic used to make bags, bottles, and packaging

collocations.example: The store packs vegetables in a thin polyethylene bag.
These food containers are made of polyethylene.

definition: to make a short sound with a horn, whistle, or similar device

collocations.example: The driver tooted the horn to warn the children.
The small train tooted loudly as it left the station.

definition: a tight piece of underwear worn around the waist and hips to shape the body

collocations.example: She wore a girdle under her dress for a smoother look.
The tight girdle made it hard for her to breathe.

definition: to cut off a branch or part of something with one quick stroke

collocations.example: The gardener lopped off the dead branch with a saw.
We lopped back the bushes along the narrow path.

definition: a serious disease that makes the muscles stiff, often caused by a dirty wound

collocations.example: The nurse gave him a tetanus shot after the injury.
You can get tetanus from a rusty nail.

definition: a chemical that an animal produces to affect the behavior of others of its kind

collocations.example: Some insects release a pheromone to attract a mate.
Ants follow a pheromone signal to find food.

definition: a chess piece shaped like a castle tower that moves in straight lines

collocations.example: She moved the rook across the board to protect the king.
He captured a rook with his bishop in one move.

definition: fat under the skin that makes it look lumpy, often on the thighs and hips

collocations.example: The cream claims to reduce cellulite on the legs.
Many people have visible cellulite and it is completely normal.

definition: a person who cares too much about small rules and details

collocations.example: He is a real pedant about correct grammar.
I don't want to sound like a pedant, but that is wrong.

definition: relating to the shape and physical features of the land in an area

collocations.example: Hikers used a topographical map to plan the route.
Engineers did a topographical survey before building the road.

definition: a mathematical expression that adds together terms made of numbers and variables

collocations.example: Students learned to solve a polynomial in algebra class.
The teacher wrote a polynomial equation on the board.

definition: looking tired and thin, usually because of worry, illness, or lack of sleep

collocations.example: She looked haggard after working three night shifts.
His haggard face showed how little he had slept.

definition: full of twists, turns, and bends

collocations.example: The bus slowly climbed the tortuous mountain road.
The river follows a tortuous course through the valley.

definition: the ability of different systems or products to work together

collocations.example: The update will improve interoperability between the two systems.
We tested the interoperability between devices from different brands.

definition: a medical examination of the inside of the large intestine using a thin camera

collocations.example: Doctors advised him to have a colonoscopy after fifty.
A routine colonoscopy can help detect problems early.

definition: a short introduction at the beginning of a book, often written by someone else

collocations.example: A famous author wrote the foreword to her novel.
The editor thanked her team in the foreword.

definition: a dull gray metal made mostly of tin, used for cups, plates, and ornaments

collocations.example: He drank cider from an old pewter mug.
The small statue was made of pewter.

definition: describing a type of fat, found in some oils and fish, that is better for health

collocations.example: Fish contains polyunsaturated fat that is good for the heart.
She cooks with polyunsaturated oil instead of butter.

definition: a collection of documents and information about a person, event, or subject

collocations.example: The reporter compiled a dossier on the company's finances.
Police kept a detailed dossier on the suspect.

definition: very dirty and unpleasant, especially because of poverty or neglect

collocations.example: The refugees lived in squalid conditions for months.
The abandoned house looked squalid and smelled awful.

definition: a particular level or class within a society

collocations.example: People from every social stratum attended the public meeting.
The reforms mainly helped a lower stratum of society.

definition: a firm yellow or white cheese with a strong taste

collocations.example: She grated some sharp cheddar over the pasta.
He put a slice of cheddar on his sandwich.

definition: the state of not being respected or trusted by people

collocations.example: The old method has fallen into disrepute among doctors.
His behavior brought the whole team into disrepute.

definition: to help or encourage someone to do something wrong, especially a crime

collocations.example: She was accused of helping to aid and abet the thieves.
Anyone who abets a crime can also be punished.
